name: Clascoterone

track.title: Lab & animal
track.line: Blocks androgen signals in scalp cells (2019)

track.title: Phase III
track.line: Hair: SCALP1 and SCALP2 done; results not posted

track.title: Hair-loss approval
track.line: Not approved for hair loss anywhere found

what.text: Clascoterone (cortexolone 17α-propionate) is a steroid that blocks the androgen receptor in the skin. It does not lower testosterone or DHT; it stops them from acting on the receptor where it is applied. FDA's label says how this helps acne is unknown.

In lab-grown human scalp cells (dermal papilla cells), clascoterone blocked androgen-driven gene activity about as well as finasteride, and lowered a DHT-driven inflammatory signal (IL-6) more than enzalutamide. This is a cell study by the developer's scientists.

src.label: Rosette et al., J Drugs Dermatol

what.text: It is sold as Winlevi 1% cream for acne. A stronger 5% solution has been tested for male pattern hair loss.

research.text: For acne, two Phase 3 trials in 1,440 people supported FDA approval. For hair loss, two Phase 3 trials (SCALP1 and SCALP2) in about 1,465 men are finished, but no results are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov and no peer-reviewed paper was found.

research.meta: US and Europe · 2023 to 2026 · Randomized Phase III
research.title: SCALP1 and SCALP2, clascoterone 5% solution

facts.v: two randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled Phase 3 trials: 6 months double-blind, then 6 months single-blind
men 18 and older with androgenetic alopecia: 703 in SCALP1, 762 in SCALP2
clascoterone 5% solution on the scalp, or vehicle (an inactive solution)
change in non-vellus hair count in the target area, and men's own rating of hair coverage, at 6 months

research.found: Both trials are listed as completed (SCALP2 in July 2025, SCALP1 in January 2026). No results are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov, and the search found no peer-reviewed results. Sponsor: Cassiopea.

research.meta: US and Europe · 2020 · Two randomized Phase III trials
research.title: Winlevi cream for facial acne (Hebert et al.)

facts.v: two identical, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled Phase 3 trials (CB-03-01/25 and /26)
1,440 males and non-pregnant females aged 9 and older with moderate or severe facial acne
clascoterone 1% cream or vehicle cream on the face twice a day
treatment success (clear or almost clear, with a 2-grade improvement) and lesion counts

research.found: Treatment success was 18.4% and 20.3% with clascoterone vs 9.0% and 6.5% with vehicle. Some authors are employed by Cassiopea, the developer.

us.text: FDA approved clascoterone as Winlevi 1% cream on August 26, 2020, for acne in people 12 and older. No clascoterone product is FDA approved for hair loss; the solution for hair loss is still investigational. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: NDA 213433, Sun Pharmaceutical. A prescription cream for acne vulgaris in patients 12 years and older.
clascoterone 5% solution has finished two Phase 3 trials (NCT05910450, NCT05914805). The search found no FDA approval for hair loss. Using the acne cream on the scalp would be off-label.

us.text: Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved. FDA does not verify their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are marketed.

world.lead: Clascoterone cream is an approved acne medicine in the US (2020), Canada and the EU (2025), and has Australian Product Information. No country was found that approves it for hair loss.

countries.status: Approved medicine: Winlevi cream (2020) for acne, age 12+. Prescription-only. Not approved for hair loss.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Clascoterone is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027. It is approved for human use, so class S0 (non-approved substances) does not cover it.

side.text: Winlevi cream mostly causes skin reactions where it is put on. Because it is a steroid absorbed into the body, it can also suppress the adrenal glands (HPA axis) and raise potassium. Safety of the 5% hair-loss solution has not been published.

items.text: in the 12-week acne trials, redness occurred in 12.2% on Winlevi vs 15.4% on vehicle, scaling or dryness in 10.5% vs 10.4%, and itching in 7.7% vs 8.2%. Skin thinning (atrophy), stretch marks and small visible blood vessels were also seen at similar rates.

in a 2-week study, signs of HPA axis suppression appeared in 1 of 20 adults (5%) and 2 of 22 adolescents (9%). All returned to normal 4 weeks after stopping. The label says children may be more susceptible.
potassium rose from normal to high in 5% of people on clascoterone vs 4% on vehicle; hyperkalemia is listed as an adverse reaction.
there are no human data. In rats and rabbits given injected clascoterone, malformations and pregnancy loss rose. EMA says Winlevi must not be used during pregnancy.
no safety results for the 5% solution are posted or published.

unconfirmed: The brand name Breezula for the hair-loss solution was not found on a regulator or registry record opened for this page; the registry calls it clascoterone solution.
Topline results of SCALP1 and SCALP2 have not been posted on ClinicalTrials.gov or published in a journal found by the search.
A 2019 paper said clascoterone was in a 'large phase 2' hair-loss trial; only one Phase 2 hair-loss trial (95 men) was found on ClinicalTrials.gov.
MHRA's product database needs a browser and GOV.UK search found no record, so UK status is not confirmed.
Australia's Product Information document sits behind a licence page and was not opened, so approved Australian uses were not checked.
surprises: Both Phase 3 hair-loss trials of clascoterone are listed as completed, the later one in January 2026, yet no results are posted on the trial registry as of November 1, 2026.
Although it is a cream, the US label warns it can suppress the adrenal glands and raise potassium.
